`UseAuthentication()`/`UseAuthorization()` are added, but nothing requires an authenticated user or the `RequireSyncReadWrite` policy before `UseCoreSyncHttpServer()`. With `Auth:UseEntraId=true` the sync server still accepts unauthenticated requests. With Entra enabled in production, any client that sends no Authorization header (or an invalid or expired token, which only fails authentication) can call the CoreSync endpoints. It can then download or upload every synced table (UserProfile, VocabularyWord, Conversation, etc.). `UseAuthorization` has no endpoint metadata to enforce, and the `RequireSyncReadWrite` policy is registered but never used. A gate is needed, e.g. `app.UseWhen(isSyncPath, b => b.Use(... if !User.Identity.IsAuthenticated -> 401 / AuthorizeAsync(policy)))`.

`GetValue<bool>("Auth:UseEntraId")` defaults to false when the key is missing. In that case DevAuthHandler is registered in every environment, including Production, so every request is authenticated as `dev-user`. The same applies to SentenceStudio.Web. appsettings.json is gitignored, so a deployed API or Web with no explicit `Auth__UseEntraId` (or a typo in the key) silently runs DevAuthHandler. Every anonymous caller then passes `.RequireAuthorization()` as dev-user/dev-tenant and can call the AI, speech and vocabulary endpoints. The setup should fail closed, e.g. throw at startup when `!useEntraId && !builder.Environment.IsDevelopment()`.

The middleware reads the short JWT claim names `tid` and `oid`. JwtBearer's default inbound claim mapping (`MapInboundClaims=true`, left on by AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApi) renames these to the `http://schemas.microsoft.com/identity/claims/tenantid` and `/objectidentifier` URIs, so the lookups return null. With a real Entra v2 access token, `FindFirstValue("tid")` returns null and the `tenant_id` fallback is also missing, so TenantId is null. `FindFirstValue("oid")` returns null too, so UserId falls back to NameIdentifier, which is the pairwise `sub` instead of the intended oid. The vocabulary status endpoint keys data by this UserId. Fix by setting `MapInboundClaims=false` on the JwtBearerOptions, or by reading the mapped URIs (`ClaimConstants.TenantId`/`ObjectId`).

The four scope policies are registered, but every endpoint uses plain `.RequireAuthorization()`. In Entra mode any token for the API audience is accepted, whatever its scopes or roles. Entra issues app-only (client-credentials) tokens for `api://8c05.../.default` to any service principal in the tenant unless assignment is required. Such a token has no `scp` or `roles`, yet passes authorization on /ai/chat, /speech/synthesize, and so on, so a stranger's daemon app can spend the OpenAI/ElevenLabs keys. A token issued with only `user.read` can also call the AI endpoints.

The AppHost sets the environment variable `Auth__UseEntraId=false` on the API. Environment variables override appsettings*.json, so the documented step "flip Auth:UseEntraId to true" in appsettings has no effect under AppHost or Aspire-based deployment. A developer sets `"UseEntraId": true` in appsettings.Development.json (or appsettings.json) and runs through AppHost. The API still registers DevAuthHandler, and all requests authenticate as dev-user. If the AppHost is used to publish, production also ships in DevAuth mode. This should be an AppHost parameter, or the hardcoded env var should be removed.

Only the `api` resource gets the `Auth__UseEntraId` and `AzureAd__*` environment variables. The `web` CoreSync server, which now has the same auth switch, gets nothing, so the two servers' auth modes can drift and Web has no AzureAd config outside Development. If Web is switched to Entra mode in a non-Development environment (where appsettings.Development.json isn't loaded and appsettings.json is gitignored), AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApi has no ClientId/Instance and fails on the first token validation (IDW10106). Separately, flipping the API to Entra via AppHost leaves Web in DevAuth mode.

`RequireUserRead`/`RequireAiAccess`/... are registered only when `useEntraId` is true, and DevAuthHandler emits no `scp` claim. The decision doc's planned next step (apply the policies to endpoints) will therefore break dev mode. Once an endpoint uses `.RequireAuthorization("RequireAiAccess")`, dev mode (`UseEntraId=false`) throws `InvalidOperationException: The AuthorizationPolicy named 'RequireAiAccess' was not found`. Even if the policies were registered, dev requests would get 403 because DevAuthHandler has no `scp`. Also, the MAUI handler only requests user.read/sync.readwrite, so real clients would get 403 on ai.access endpoints. The same pattern applies to `RequireSyncReadWrite` in SentenceStudio.Web.

Neither DevAuthApiFactory nor JwtBearerApiFactory sets `Auth:UseEntraId`. Both rely on whatever ambient config the machine has (a local gitignored appsettings.json or environment variables). A developer has a local appsettings.json with `Auth:UseEntraId=true`, as the decision doc says exists. Microsoft.Identity.Web then registers the `Bearer` scheme, and JwtBearerApiFactory's `AddJwtBearer("Bearer")` throws `InvalidOperationException: Scheme already exists: Bearer`. The DevAuth tests also return 401 instead of 200. Use `builder.UseSetting("Auth:UseEntraId", "false")` in both factories.

The generated token adds `tenant_id` and `ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier`, which real Entra tokens never carry. `API_ExtractsTenantContext` passes through the DevAuth fallback branch, and the `tid`/`oid` branch is never exercised. JwtBearer maps the test token's `tid`/`oid` to long URIs, so the middleware's `tid`/`oid` lookups return null. The test still passes because the `tenant_id` and NameIdentifier fallbacks hold the same values. This masks the production bug where TenantId is null and UserId is `sub`. The token should contain only real Entra claims (tid, oid, sub, name, preferred_username, scp).

The factory keeps the DevAuth branch of Program.cs and layers a plain AddJwtBearer on top. The production branch (AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApi, its claim handling and the RequireScope policies) never runs in tests, despite the comment saying it "simulates the production Entra ID auth path". Regressions specific to the Entra branch pass CI: misconfigured AzureAd binding, Microsoft.Identity.Web claim mapping, the missing policies, or a startup exception. Setting `Auth:UseEntraId=true` and post-configuring `JwtBearerOptions` for the `Bearer` scheme (signing key, issuer, audience) would exercise the real registration.

SentenceStudio.Api.Tests is not added to src/SentenceStudio.sln, and .github/workflows/test.yml only builds and runs SentenceStudio.UnitTests, so none of the new auth tests ever run in CI. A later change that breaks JWT rejection, for example `API_RejectsUnauthenticatedGetRequest` starting to return 200, merges with a green check because the project is never built or tested by the PR workflow.

Email falls back to `preferred_username`. Microsoft documents that claim as a mutable display hint that may be a UPN, a phone number, or a non-routable alias, not a verified email. For a user whose UPN is `jdoe@contoso.onmicrosoft.com`, or for a phone-sign-in account, `/auth/bootstrap` returns that value as Email. Anything that sends mail to it, or matches profiles by email, gets the wrong address. Email should stay null unless an `email` claim is present.

The middleware now carries two claim vocabularies (Entra `tid`/`oid`/`name` plus DevAuth `tenant_id`/NameIdentifier/Name) as `??` chains. The bootstrap endpoint repeats a third, partial fallback (`?? user.FindFirstValue("tenant_id")`). Every new claim needs dual-path lookups, and the two paths already disagree: bootstrap falls back to `tenant_id` but not `tid`. A simpler fix is to have DevAuthHandler emit the Entra claim names (tid, oid, name, preferred_username, scp), turn off inbound mapping, read one set of names in the middleware, and drop the bootstrap fallbacks.

DevAuthHandler is copied verbatim from SentenceStudio.Api/Auth/DevAuthHandler.cs, and the whole `if (useEntraId) ... else ...` registration block is duplicated in Web's Program.cs. In Web's dev mode the synthetic identity has no consumer, because CoreSync never reads `HttpContext.User`. The two copies are already set to drift (claim names, policy lists). Any fix to one auth path, such as fail-closed in production or MapInboundClaims, has to be made twice. Moving DevAuthHandler and an `AddSentenceStudioAuthentication(builder)` extension into the shared ServiceDefaults project would leave one implementation.

The AzureAd Instance, TenantId, ClientId and Audience literals are repeated in AppHost env vars and in both appsettings.Development.json files, on top of the copies in MsalAuthService and AuthenticatedHttpMessageHandler. Rotating or re-registering the Entra app means editing five or more places. Missing one, e.g. the Web appsettings, leaves that server rejecting the new audience. The AppHost env vars only duplicate what appsettings.Development.json already provides. Define the values once (AppHost parameters passed to both projects) and drop the duplicates.

`_AndroidRunNativeCompile` now has `DependsOnTargets="_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesignerUpdateItems;…"`, but that target only exists in Microsoft.Android.Sdk.TypeMap.LlvmIr.targets. That file is not imported when `_AndroidTypeMapImplementation == 'trimmable'`. A NativeAOT app built with `_AndroidTypeMapImplementation=trimmable` (a supported pairing: Trimmable.targets imports Trimmable.NativeAOT.targets). Xamarin.Android.Common.targets:2878-2881 imports only Trimmable.targets. The inner build reaches `_AndroidRunNativeCompile` (no condition, runs after ComputeResolvedFilesToPublishList) and fails with MSB4057 "target _PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesignerUpdateItems does not exist", in every configuration.

The swap only rewrites `ResolvedFileToPublish`. For NativeAOT, the ILC package's `_ComputeManagedAssemblyForILLink` rebuilds `ManagedAssemblyToLink` from `_ManagedResolvedAssembliesToPublish`, which comes from `_ResolvedCopyLocalPublishAssets` (the comment at line 401-407 notes this replacement). So ILLink still trims the original, un-rewritten libraries. The post-trim FixLegacy step that used to exist was deleted. A NativeAOT release app references a legacy-designer library (old AndroidX or Xamarin.Forms package). PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner writes prelink/Lib.dll, but ILLink/ILC consume the NuGet-cache Lib.dll. The library keeps `ldsfld Lib.Resource/Layout::X` with library-local IDs and no UpdateIdValues, so wrong resource IDs are used at runtime. Also, ILLink's `ResolvedFileToPublish Remove="@(ManagedAssemblyToLink)"` doesn't match the prelink paths, so the prelink items leak into ResolvedFileToPublish next to the linked copies. apkdesc sizes and the device test (which only prints Foo.Hello) can't tell the difference.

`_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesignerUpdateItems` swaps in any `prelink/<name>.dll` that exists on disk, not the set the task produced for the current inputs. The task never clears the directory or removes copies for assemblies it no longer modifies, and Clean doesn't remove `prelink/`. Build 1: library Foo 1.0 has a legacy designer, so prelink/Foo.dll is written. The user then updates to Foo 2.0, which has no legacy designer (`ProcessAssemblyDesigner` returns false), or the designer fails to resolve. The task reruns, doesn't write Foo, and leaves the old file. The swap then replaces Foo 2.0 with the rewritten Foo 1.0 copy. The app ships old library code, and dependants compiled against 2.0 can hit MissingMethodException or TypeLoadException.

`Inputs="@(_PreTrimmingAssembly)"` with only a stamp as output detects newer timestamps only. Adding an assembly, or switching to one with older file times, doesn't rerun the task. Neither do property or task-assembly changes. Other targets in this repo add `$(_AndroidBuildPropertiesCache)` or a resolved-assemblies hash for this reason. NuGet keeps zip-entry timestamps on extraction. After a successful build, the user adds a legacy-designer package whose DLL dates are older than the stamp, or downgrades Foo 2.0 to Foo 1.0 that is already in the cache. `_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner` is skipped. The new library isn't rewritten (wrong resource IDs at runtime), or the downgraded Foo is replaced by the stale rewritten prelink copy of 2.0.

The deleted `PostTrimmingFixLegacyResourceDesignerStep` deliberately ran on every assembly ("matching the behavior of the former ILLink path which processed all assemblies without StepContext flag filtering"). The new task skips the main assembly, so release builds no longer rewrite app-side reads of legacy library Resource fields. App code reads `SomeLib.Resource.Layout.Foo` directly (compiled as `ldsfld SomeLib.Resource/Layout::Foo`). The library is processed and `ClearDesignerClass(completely: true)` removes its nested types. Before, the main assembly hit the unresolved-member fallback (`_Linker.Generated.Resource`) and was redirected to the designer getter. Now it is skipped, so ILLink sees an unresolved field and the app throws MissingFieldException at runtime.

The pre-trim designer fix doesn't depend on the typemap, but it lives in the LlvmIr typemap file and patches `ResolvedFileToPublish`. NativeAOT then needs a special-case DependsOn. The trimmable typemap path never gets the fix, and NativeAOT's ILLink input path is missed. Each ILLink entry path (MonoVM/CoreCLR, NativeAOT, trimmable typemap) needs its own wiring, and two of three are broken (see the MSB4057 and NativeAOT findings). A simpler fix: move these targets to shared targets (e.g. Xamarin.Android.Resource.Designer.targets) and swap `ManagedAssemblyToLink` right before `_RunILLink`, after both `_ComputeManagedAssemblyToLink` and `_ComputeManagedAssemblyForILLink`. That covers every ILLink caller with no runtime-specific hook.

Only `.dll` items are moved to `prelink/`. The SDK's `_PDBToLink` pairs PDBs with `ManagedAssemblyToLink` by `%(RelativeDir)%(Filename).pdb`, so the original PDB in the NuGet or obj folder no longer matches the prelink DLL. The PDB the task writes to `prelink/` isn't added to ResolvedFileToPublish either. In a release build with symbols included (AndroidIncludeDebugSymbols=true, or TrimmerRemoveSymbols off), the original Foo.pdb is no longer seen as a linked PDB. It stays in ResolvedFileToPublish and ships next to the trimmed, rewritten Foo.dll. Symbolication or debugging uses a PDB whose IL offsets and MVID don't match.

`FileWrites` is filled from the task's `ModifiedAssemblies` output, which can't be inferred when the target is skipped, so it is empty on no-op builds. It also leaves out the `.pdb` files written to `prelink/`, and `_CleanMonoAndroidIntermediateDir` doesn't remove the `prelink` directory. On an incremental build where `_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner` is skipped, the prelink DLLs aren't in FileWrites, so an IncrementalClean pass treats them as orphans. Meanwhile `clean` never removes `prelink/*.pdb` or the directory itself. The leftover copies feed the Exists()-based swap (stale prelink finding).

If `_Microsoft.Android.Resource.Designer` can't be resolved from the collected search directories, `ProcessAssemblyDesigner` returns false with only a debug-level "Not using …" message. The task succeeds and touches the stamp, and the root descriptor safety net has been removed. Designer resolution only works if the designer DLL sits next to some collected assembly (today via `_FixupIntermediateAssembly`). Under NativeAOT, `_AndroidRunNativeCompile` runs before `_AddResourceDesignerToPublishFiles`. If those paths diverge, every legacy library is left unfixed with no warning, and the stamp then suppresses reruns. Users get wrong resource IDs at runtime instead of a build error.

The inline main/framework filter claims to "match the filtering in FixLegacyResourceDesignerStep.ProcessAssembly", but that method filters `IsMainAssembly || !IsAndroidUserAssembly`, which is narrower. The task also duplicates resolver setup from PostTrimmingPipeline and write logic that `SaveChangedAssemblyStep` already provides (write if modified, copy otherwise). Two filter definitions now drift apart: non-Android user libraries are processed here but not in LinkAssembliesNoShrink. Reusing `StepContext` plus `fixLegacyStep.ProcessAssembly` (or `SaveChangedAssemblyStep`, which writes every destination) would also fix the stale prelink problem.

`ModifiedAssemblies`, `CopyMetadataTo`, and the `OriginalPath` metadata are consumed only by `FileWrites`. The swap target re-derives the modified set from `Exists()` checks instead. Dead metadata and two sources of truth for "which assemblies were rewritten". Persisting the list (e.g. WriteLinesToFile as the target Output, ReadLinesFromFile in UpdateItems) would replace both and remove the stale-file risk.

`_CollectPreTrimmingAssemblies` and `_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner` both declare `AfterTargets="ComputeResolvedFilesToPublishList"`, but they are already pulled in through the DependsOnTargets chain of `_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesignerUpdateItems`. The same three-part Condition is copied on all three targets. Extra scheduling edges make ordering harder to reason about (NativeAOT already needed a manual DependsOn fix). The duplicated conditions can drift. One AfterTargets on the leaf target plus a shared property for the condition does the same job.

The resolver is created with `loadDebugSymbols: true`, so symbols are read for every non-framework assembly scanned, though nearly all have no legacy designer and are never written. Each rerun (any input touched, including the designer DLL after a resource edit) reads PDBs for every NuGet library just to check custom attributes and member refs. Loading symbols only for assemblies about to be written (or `ReadSymbols` on demand) avoids that I/O.

No test checks that the linked output actually contains the rewritten designer-getter calls, that a no-op build skips `_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner` but still swaps, or the NativeAOT and trimmable typemap paths. apkdesc size drops look the same whether libraries were fixed or the designer was just trimmed. The device test `FixLegacyResourceDesignerStep` only logs `Foo.Hello` without checking its value. The NativeAOT, stale-file, and incremental bugs above can all pass CI.

Phase 4.5 (and PO amendments under Rule 5) rewrite the story file after Phase 4.1 wrote tasks-story-XXXX-YYYY.md, so mtime(story) > mtime(tasks) on every completed run and the RULE-002 freshness check can never pass. Run /x-story-plan story-0028-0002 to completion, then run it again with no edits: Phase 0.3 sees mtime(story) > mtime(tasks), logs 'Regenerating stale story plan' and relaunches all 5 agents. The guard checks the lead's own cwd and branch (`git symbolic-ref HEAD`, `process.cwd()/.dev-team/.reviews`), not the target implementer's worktree or branch, so it does nothing in the scenario it was built for. When the lead sends shutdown_request to `voss-implement`, the hook resolves branch=`main` and exits 0 at line 93, so the premature shutdown from #795 still goes through. If the lead happens to be on some other feature branch, it checks that branch's sidecars, and one implementer's review can unblock shutdown of every implementer.

Evidence matching only looks for the sanitized branch in the sidecar filename, but ADR-029 sidecars are named `<agent>--<content-hash>.json` and never contain the branch. The JSON `branch` field that merge-gate matches on is never read. Knuth reviews `feat/123-x` and writes `.dev-team/.reviews/knuth--a1b2c3d4e5f6.json` with `{"branch":"feat/123-x"}`. `f.includes("feat-123-x")` is false for every real sidecar, so whenever the guard runs on a feature branch it blocks shutdown even after review, and users fall back to `--force-shutdown` every time.

Config handling only treats `workflow.review === false` as disabled, but `review` is a `WorkflowToggle` (`boolean | "complex"`). With `"complex"`, SIMPLE tasks get no review, and the guard blocks their implementers' shutdown indefinitely. config.json has `workflow: { review: "complex" }`. A SIMPLE task is implemented with no review by design, so no sidecars exist. The lead's shutdown_request to `voss-implement-42` exits 2 every time, and only `--force-shutdown` gets past it. The guard should read `.dev-team/.assessments/<branch>.json` and skip non-COMPLEX branches.

The existence of any sidecar is used as a stand-in for "all review findings routed and acknowledged" (the #795 requirement). The first sidecar from any reviewer, round, or LIGHT advisory pass unblocks shutdown, even though findings haven't been delivered yet. Szabo writes its sidecar with 2 [DEFECT] findings that the lead hasn't routed yet, and Knuth/Brooks are still running. The lead sends shutdown_request and the guard allows it because one sidecar exists, which is exactly the premature shutdown the task skill forbids. Stale sidecars are never cleaned up (ADR-043 retention note), so evidence from an earlier round also satisfies the guard.

`f.includes(sanitizedBranch)` is a substring match, so shorter branch names match sidecars from longer branches. Sanitization also maps different branches to the same name (`feat/a.b` and `feat/a-b` both become `feat-a-b`). Branch `fix/12` (sanitized `fix-12`) has no review, but an old sidecar `knuth--fix-123-foo.json` from `fix/123` is still in `.reviews/`. `"knuth--fix-123-foo.json".includes("fix-12")` is true, so shutdown of the unreviewed `fix/12` implementer is allowed.

Any plain-text SendMessage whose body contains the substring `shutdown_request` is treated as a shutdown and can be blocked, even when it's ordinary conversation. The lead sends `voss-implement` the string "Reviews pending — do not respond to any shutdown_request until Knuth finishes". `message.includes("shutdown_request")` is true, so the normal message is blocked with "Cannot shut down" and the instruction never arrives.

The hook only accepts the `tool_input.to` / `tool_input.message` shape. If SendMessage carries `type: "shutdown_request"` and `recipient` at the top level (the agent-teams schema variant), `message` is undefined and the guard exits 0 without any check. SendMessage input `{type:"shutdown_request", recipient:"voss-implement", content:"done"}` → `input.tool_input.message` is undefined → `process.exit(0)` at line 40 → no enforcement, with no warning. Reading `tool_input.type`/`recipient` as fallbacks would cover both shapes.

Using `/implement/i` on the free-form teammate name gets it wrong both ways. Qualifiers can contain "implement", so reviewers get guarded, while implementers named outside the convention (or a `*` broadcast) skip the check. `knuth-review-implementer-guard` (role=review, qualifier=feature name, which the convention allows) matches `/implement/i`, so shutting down the reviewer is blocked. An implementer spawned as `voss-773` or `builder` doesn't match, so its premature shutdown is allowed.

CLAUDE.md (repo root) says templates must be "**Workflow-agnostic** — don't assume PRs, specific branch naming, or any particular development workflow". In a project whose trunk is `develop` or `trunk`, a lead on trunk is treated as being on a feature branch and gets blocked on every implementer shutdown. The sidecar scan has no `lstat` regular-file and symlink filtering. merge-gate added exactly that in the immediately preceding commit (#769), so here a symlink or directory named `*<branch>*.json` counts as review evidence. An agent or a stray `mkdir .dev-team/.reviews/x--feat-123-test.json` (a directory) or a symlink with a matching name satisfies `f.endsWith(".json")` and unblocks shutdown with no review content. merge-gate would reject the same entry, so the two gates disagree.

The "allows with review evidence" test uses a made-up sidecar name `knuth--feat-123-test.json` instead of the ADR-029 `<agent>--<hash>.json` format, and every test runs with the hook's cwd on the feature branch. That hides the two main bugs. The suite passes, but in production the guard always blocks (real sidecar names) or never fires (lead on `main`/implementer in a worktree). There are no tests for: lead on main, detached HEAD, a sidecar for another or prefix-colliding branch, `review: "complex"`, plain-text messages mentioning shutdown_request, or reviewer names containing "implement".

If the bypass warning is removed or broken, the "allows --force-shutdown bypass" test still passes. The merge-gate tests at line 2474 switched to `spawnSync` for exactly this reason ("to capture stderr even on exit 0").

Branch sanitization and sidecar-for-branch lookup are written inline again here. merge-gate already has `sanitizeBranch()` plus `branch`-field and symlink-aware matching.
